authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: Wise completed its Nasdaq listing and moved its primary listing there. Wise Group plc became the ultimate parent of Wise Limited through a Scheme of Arrangement.

Wise announced a share buyback program and expects to repurchase up to £405 million (approximately $540 million) of Class A ordinary shares. Weekly 6-K filings show repurchases under it are continuing, with the shares held in treasury.
Wise Europe, its Belgian subsidiary, reached an agreement to settle the matter raised by the Brussels prosecutor's office, with no admission of wrongdoing.

business_model.claim: Wise sells cross-border money services through three offerings: Wise Account for individuals, Wise Business for small and medium-sized businesses, and Wise Platform for banks, financial institutions and enterprises.
quotes: We market our services through three product offerings: Wise Account for personal customers, Wise Business for small and medium-sized businesses, and Wise Platform for banks, financial institutions and enterprises.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (Item 5); the absence of formal segments is inferred from this wording
business_model.claim: The filing does not report by product offering. Revenue is evaluated and managed by net revenue stream, and the evidence does not name any formal reporting segments. Wise Business was about one quarter of transaction activity, and Wise Platform is included within the Account and Business activity at under 10%.
quotes: We evaluate and manage our revenue principally based on these net revenue streams rather than by individual product offerings.
it currently generates less than 10%

business_model.claim: Net revenue is built from three lines. Transaction revenue is the largest. Interest income on customer balances is a second source, reduced by interest paid back to customers. Table in millions: transaction revenue 1,893.6, interest income 806.1, interest expense 196.9 (deducted), net revenue 2,502.8 for the year to March 31, 2026.

Transaction revenue comes mainly from fees on cross-border volume. Cross-border revenue divided by volume gives the take rate. Volume rose to $243.5 billion from $185.2 billion, while the average take rate fell to 0.52% from 0.58%.
quotes: Cross-border take rate is calculated as cross-border revenue divided by cross-border volume.

business_model.claim: Volume growth is underpinned by growth in active customers, from 15.6 million to 18.9 million.
quotes: Growth in cross-border volume over these periods was underpinned by growth in active customers, which increased from 15.6 million in the financial year ended March 31, 2025 to 18.9 million in the financial year ended March 31, 2026.

business_model.claim: Card revenue, mainly interchange and card usage fees, was 16% of net revenue in the year.
quotes: which was 16% for the financial year ended March 31, 2026

business_model.claim: Interest income depends on the size of customer deposits and on market interest rates. Wise aims to return 80% of interest yield above 1% to customers but returned 45% of that target, so interest expense on customer liabilities could grow if more is returned.
quotes: Interest income on customer balances is affected by the amount of customer deposits we hold and market interest rates.
We returned 45% of this target in the financial year ended March 31, 2026

business_model.basis: stated in the balance sheet; the link to interest income is inferred from Item 5
business_model.claim: Customer money dominates the balance sheet. Table in millions: funds payable and amounts due to customers of 30,254.2 against total assets of 33,259.8, with cash and cash equivalents of 27,802.2 and shareholders' equity of 1,925.2 at March 31, 2026.
Costs rose faster than revenue in the year. Table in millions: total operating expenses were 1,912.1 against 1,370.7, up 39%, while net revenue rose 19%. Operating income fell to 590.7 from 728.2.
quotes: This was accompanied by increased investment in headcount, servicing, third-party spend and outsourced services

business_model.claim: The largest cost line is transaction expense, the cost of processing and settling payments and providing cards. Table in millions: 513.6 against 378.0, up 36%.
quotes: Transaction expense (excluding depreciation and amortization) consists of the costs incurred by Wise in processing and settlement of transactions as well as providing debit card services.

business_model.claim: Wise says it passes efficiency gains and cost reductions to customers as lower prices, which lowers the take rate. It also says that if its costs rise it may need to raise fees, which could make it less competitive.
quotes: Our commitment to a return-led approach means we continue to pass on efficiency gains and sustainable reductions in our costs to our customers as price reductions, driving our long-term growth and reducing our take rate.

business_model.claim: In the half-year report for H1 FY27, net revenue was 1,453.1 ($ million) against 1,183.8 a year earlier, a 23% rise. The cross-border take rate was 0.50% against 0.52%, and cross-border volume was $141.0 billion.
quotes: Net revenue ($ million) | 1,453.1 | 1,183.8 | 23%
Cross-border take rate (%) | 0.50% | 0.52% | -2 bps

competitive_position.claim: Wise is growing at scale. Cross-border volume reached $243.5 billion in FY2026, up from $185.2 billion, and active customers rose to 18.9 million from 15.6 million.
quotes: In the financial year ended March 31, 2026, our cross-border volume was $243.5 billion, up from $185.2 billion in the financial year ended March 31, 2025.

competitive_position.claim: Price is Wise's main competitive lever. The average cross-border take rate fell from 0.58% to 0.52%, and the company says the cuts support growth in volume and customers.
quotes: Our cross-border take rate decreased from an average of 0.58% for the financial year ended March 31, 2025 to 0.52% for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, with personal customer cross-border take rates decreasing from 0.63% to 0.57% and business customer cross-border take rates decreasing from 0.44% to 0.39%.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 20-F text and the income statement.
competitive_position.claim: The price-led strategy and heavier investment coincided with lower profit. Net income fell by $51.6 million to $498.7 million, and operating income fell from 728.2 to 590.7 (table in millions) because operating expenses rose faster than net revenue.
quotes: Our net income was $498.7 million for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, a decline of $51.6 million over the financial year ended March 31, 2025, primarily driven by the reduction in our average cross-border take rate by 0.06 percentage points, from 0.58% to 0.52%, reducing net revenue growth compared to volume growth.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 20-F Item 4 text; the edge itself is the company's own claim.
competitive_position.claim: Wise's infrastructure is a stated source of advantage. It held over 80 licences and routed over half of all transactions through direct connections to domestic payment systems, which it says lets it speed up payments and cut costs.
quotes: This speed is driven in part by routing over half of all transactions in the period through our connections to domestic payment systems.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the income statement and the 20-F Item 5 text.
competitive_position.claim: Customer balances give Wise a second income stream but tie results to interest rates. Interest income on customer balances was 806.1 against interest expense on customer liabilities of 196.9 (table in millions). Wise returned 45% of its interest-return target in FY2026, and its interest expense may grow if it returns more.
quotes: Interest income on customer balances is affected by the amount of customer deposits we hold and market interest rates.
We returned 45% of this target in the financial year ended March 31, 2026

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 20-F text and the 6-K; the 50% figure is an aim, not a result.
competitive_position.claim: Wise Platform, the bank-partner channel, is still small but is a strategic aim. It generates less than 10% of transaction activity, and the long-term aim is more than 50% of cross-border volume. The H1 FY27 release reports new platform partners, including two large North American banks.
quotes: Our long-term aim is for Wise Platform to account for more than 50% of Wise’s cross-border volume.
Increased Wise Platform partners with three silent launches including two large banks in North America

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 6-K release summary; parts of the release are omitted from the packet.
competitive_position.claim: Growth continued into H1 FY27. Cross-border volume was $141.0 billion, up 24% year on year, and active customers rose 21%. The take rate was 0.50% against 0.52% a year earlier.
quotes: Cross-border volume was $141.0 billion, an increase of 24% YoY (or 22% in constant currency) - this was mainly driven by strong growth in the U.S. and Asia Pacific
Active customers increased 21% YoY to over 16 million, with 4.1 million new active customers during the period

competitive_position.claim: Competition is a named threat. The market is fragmented and highly competitive, and traditional banks have larger customer bases and scale. Some face lighter licensing and capital rules and may price lower, including by cross-subsidising.
quotes: Some of our current and potential competitors, particularly traditional banks with whom we compete, have longer operating histories, as well as other potential advantages over us, including greater customer bases, volume, scale or market share, while some have less burdensome licensing, capital, liquidity and other regulatory requirements.

competitive_position.claim: Reliance on banks and payment partners limits Wise in some markets. In the US it is not eligible for card network membership and must be sponsored by a member bank. A past Brazilian partner dispute led to an investigation by Brazilian authorities.
quotes: because we are not a bank, our business is not eligible for membership in card payment networks, and we are, therefore, unable to directly access card payment networks in the United States

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the risk factors and the 6-K; the settlement terms are not given.
competitive_position.claim: Financial-crime and regulatory exposure is a named threat. Wise's products have been misused for illegal or fraudulent purposes in the past. A Belgian prosecutor matter has been settled with no admission of wrongdoing.
quotes: Our products and services have been improperly utilized for illegal, improper and fraudulent uses in the past
An agreement has now been reached to fully resolve and settle this matter, with no admission of wrongdoing

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 20-F risk factor summary; the nature of the weaknesses is not in the packet.
competitive_position.claim: The 20-F discloses material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting, which the company lists among its risks to timely and accurate reporting.
quotes: In connection with our preparation for compliance with the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, we have identified deficiencies in our internal control over financial reporting that constitute material weaknesses.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet; the reading that customer funds dominate is inferred from the line items.
financial_health.claim: Liquidity looks ample on the balance sheet. Cash and cash equivalents were 27,802.2 (table in millions) and available-for-sale debt securities were 4,582.7. Total current assets of 32,980.6 exceeded total current liabilities of 30,805.6. Most current liabilities are funds payable and amounts due to customers of 30,254.2.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet; the interpretation of customer funds versus borrowings is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Reported leverage is high, but it is mostly customer-related. Total liabilities were 31,334.6 (table in millions) against total shareholders' equity of 1,925.2. Borrowings are small by comparison: long-term debt was 328.7 and short-term debt was 6.0, against 0.0 and 128.4 a year earlier.

financial_health.basis: Figures are stated in the cash flow statement and balance sheet; the replacement link is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Debt was reshaped during the year. The cash flow statement shows proceeds from debt issuance of 328,700 (table in thousands), revolving credit facility proceeds of 267,200 and repayments of 397,900. This matches the move from short-term to long-term debt on the balance sheet.

financial_health.basis: Figures are stated in the cash flow statement; the quality judgement is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Reported operating cash flow is far larger than earnings, but it is driven by customer money. Net cash provided by operating activities was 7,553,900 (table in thousands) against net income of 498,700. The change in funds payable and amounts due to customers contributed 6,999,700.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the income statement and the operating review.
financial_health.claim: Underlying profitability weakened over the year. Operating income fell to 590.7 (table in millions) from 728.2 as total operating expenses rose to 1,912.1 from 1,370.7. Management attributes the net income decline mainly to the cross-border take rate falling to 0.52% from 0.58%.

financial_health.basis: Figures are stated in the income statement; the rate sensitivity is stated in the operating review.
financial_health.claim: A large part of revenue depends on interest earned on customer balances. Interest income on customer balances was 806.1 (table in millions), against interest expense on customer liabilities of 196.9. Management says this income depends on balances held and on market interest rates.

financial_health.basis: Figures and the programme size are stated in the cited items; how the buyback is funded is not stated.
financial_health.claim: Cash is being returned to shareholders at a faster pace. Share repurchases were 473,400 (table in thousands), against 92,500 a year earlier. The buyback announced in July allows up to £405 million (approximately $540 million), and repurchases were still being reported in November. Capital expenditure on property, plant and equipment was only 19,600.
quotes: In connection with the Buyback, the Company expects to repurchase up to £405 million (approximately $540 million) of its Class A ordinary shares.

financial_health.basis: Debt balances are stated; the low-need reading is inferred from the balances.
financial_health.claim: Refinancing needs appear modest. Debt due within a year was 6.0 (table in millions), and long-term debt of 328.7 was newly raised. Large cash and securities balances exist, but most belong to customers. No maturity dates or facility terms appear in the excerpts, so how and when debt will be repaid cannot be traced.
quotes: Other income/(loss), net consists primarily of losses on the sale or maturity of available-for-sale debt securities, interest expense related to the Revolving Credit Facility, Euro Medium Term Note and interest income earned from our corporate short-term financial instruments.

financial_health.claim: Counterparty and safeguarding risk is material to liquidity. Management says most cash on deposit exceeds government deposit insurance limits, and that it must hold and segregate at least 100% of customer funds.
quotes: We have significant amounts of cash and cash equivalents outstanding on deposit or in accounts with banks or other counterparties, the majority of which exceed applicable government deposit insurance limits.
We hold, and in certain jurisdictions are required to hold and segregate, at least 100% of the aggregate amount of all customer funds and assets held by our licensed entities.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the risk factor summary.
financial_health.claim: Management discloses material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting, which bears on how far the reported figures can be relied on.
quotes: In connection with our preparation for compliance with the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, we have identified deficiencies in our internal control over financial reporting that constitute material weaknesses.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 6-K summary table; the implication for liquidity is inferred.

Net revenue was 1,453.1 ($ million per table) against 1,183.8, and customer holdings were 43.5 ($ billion per table) against 33.9. growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the cited items; the condition is inferred from the customer-retention risk factor and the Customer Growth discussion.
growth_thesis.claim: Growth in active customers is a driver. They rose from 15.6 million to 18.9 million in FY26, and H1 FY27 active customers were up 21% to over 16 million. For this to continue, the company must keep attracting new customers in a competitive market and keep them active.
quotes: Growth in cross-border volume over these periods was underpinned by growth in active customers, which increased from 15.6 million in the financial year ended March 31, 2025 to 18.9 million in the financial year ended March 31, 2026.
Active customers increased 21% YoY to over 16 million, with 4.1 million new active customers during the period

growth_thesis.claim: Cross-border volume growth is the core revenue driver. Volume was $243.5 billion in FY26, up from $185.2 billion, and was $141.0 billion in H1 FY27, up 24% year on year. For this to continue, customer activity and volume must keep expanding, helped in the H1 FY27 report by strong growth in the U.S. and Asia Pacific.
quotes: In the financial year ended March 31, 2026, our cross-border volume was $243.5 billion, up from $185.2 billion in the financial year ended March 31, 2025.
Cross-border volume was $141.0 billion, an increase of 24% YoY (or 22% in constant currency) - this was mainly driven by strong growth in the U.S. and Asia Pacific

growth_thesis.claim: Lower prices are an explicit strategy to fuel volume and customer growth. The cross-border take rate fell from 0.58% to 0.52% in FY26 and was 0.50% in H1 FY27. For this to continue, volume growth must outweigh the falling take rate, and the company must be able to keep passing cost efficiencies on to customers.
quotes: We believe these reductions in cross-border take rates, as a result of price reductions and mix effect, have supported growth in cross-border volumes and active customers by making our products and features more attractive to customers.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the business overview; the continuation condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Direct connections to domestic payment systems are an infrastructure driver of speed and cost. For this to continue, the company must keep adding and maintaining these integrations and licences. The H1 FY27 report adds a ninth direct integration, in Malaysia.
quotes: This speed is driven in part by routing over half of all transactions in the period through our connections to domestic payment systems.
Expanded our global infrastructure with the addition of our ninth direct integration, in Malaysia

growth_thesis.claim: Licensing and onboarding capacity gate customer growth. The company states that customer growth depends on keeping existing licences, obtaining new ones, and having capacity to onboard customers.
quotes: Our customer growth is dependent on our ability to maintain existing and obtain new licenses, as well as maintaining capacity to onboard new customers.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the cited item; the mix counter is inferred from the separate personal and business take rates.
growth_thesis.claim: Wise Business is a growth driver. Business cross-border volume grew 42% since FY25, with businesses sending or spending $5.9 billion on average every month. For this to continue, the company must keep adding business customers and deepening business features and integrations.
quotes: We continue to see growth in volume with businesses having sent or spent a total of $5.9 billion on average every month in the financial year ended March 31, 2026, growing our business cross-border volumes by 42% since the financial year ended March 31, 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: The 10% and 50% figures are stated in P3; the conditions are inferred from the partner-based model and the risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: Wise Platform is positioned as a future driver, but its current share is small. The company says it currently generates less than 10% of transaction activity and aims for more than 50% of cross-border volume. For this to be realised, banks and enterprises must keep integrating Wise's infrastructure; the H1 FY27 report cites new partners such as OakNorth and Vivid.
quotes: Our long-term aim is for Wise Platform to account for more than 50% of Wise’s cross-border volume.
Added additional Wise Platform partners, including OakNorth, the digital bank for entrepreneurs, and Vivid, the European financial platform

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the cited items; the 16% share is stated in P3.
growth_thesis.claim: Card revenue is a growth driver. In H1 FY27 it rose 43% to $252.0 million on card spend of $27.2 billion, helped by business adoption of the Wise Card mainly in the U.S. For this to continue, card usage and interchange income must keep growing; card was 16% of net revenue in FY26.
quotes: Card revenue increasing 43% YoY to $252.0 million, due to increased card spend volume of 33% YoY to $27.2 billion and higher interchange fees, on average, from higher business adoption and use of the Wise Card, mainly in the U.S.

growth_thesis.basis: Balances and the rate dependence are stated in P3; the 6% and 22% growth rates are the printed variances in the P3 results table.
growth_thesis.claim: Interest income on growing customer balances supports net revenue. Business deposits were $11.2 billion versus $8.4 billion, and personal balances rose 38% to $18.8 billion. For this to continue, balances must keep growing, and market interest rates and the portion of interest returned to customers must stay supportive.
quotes: Interest income on customer balances is affected by the amount of customer deposits we hold and market interest rates.
Business customer deposits held totaled $11.2 billion at March 31, 2026 as compared to $8.4 billion at March 31, 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Growth rates are printed in the P3 results table; the condition is inferred from the cost and revenue growth gap and the stated investment plans.
growth_thesis.claim: Costs are growing faster than net revenue, so continued profit growth requires revenue growth to outpace the planned investment in headcount, marketing, servicing and infrastructure. Net revenue grew 19% in FY26 while total operating expenses grew 39%.
quotes: This was accompanied by increased investment in headcount, servicing, third-party spend and outsourced services, reflecting in part our preparation for the Reorganization Transaction and commencement of operations as a U.S. listed company, as well as continued investment in our infrastructure, marketing and product development.
